title: Best Usb-C Charger (2026)
summary: The guide highlights four USB‑C chargers that consistently deliver fast, reliable charging for a range of devices.
method: Picks were selected from the four sources provided, prioritizing products mentioned by more than one source. The Anker Nano II 65W appears in the 2026 review, and the Anker 735 Nano II 65W is highlighted in the TechGearLab testing. Apple 20W USB‑C and UGREEN Nexode 30W are noted in the 2026 roundup.
assumptions: Prices are not listed in the sources, so no price information is included.

products.name: Anker Nano II 65W
why: The Anker Nano II 65W is a GaN‑II PPS USB‑C charger that can power a MacBook Air in less than two hours, a MacBook Pro 13" at full speed, and an iPhone 13 up to three times faster than a 5W charger. It also charges Samsung phones at full speed with Samsung Super Fast Charging.
The charger is 58% smaller than a 61W USB‑C charger and features a foldable plug, making it space‑saving and portable.
products.desc: The Anker Nano II 65W is a compact GaN‑II PPS USB‑C charger that delivers up to 65W of power. It can charge a MacBook Air in under two hours, a MacBook Pro 13" at full speed, and an iPhone 13 three times faster than the stock 5W charger. It does not include a USB‑A port.
products.benefit: Picture a busy commuter who needs a single brick to power a phone, tablet and a laptop. The Anker Nano II 65W delivers that with its GaN‑II PPS technology, charging a MacBook Air in under two hours and an iPhone 13 three times faster than the stock 5W charger. It beats the other picks by providing the highest single‑brick wattage and the fastest laptop charging time. The catch: it has no USB‑A port, so older cables need a separate adapter.
pros: Fast charging for laptops and phones
cons: Requires USB‑C cable for older devices
products.best_for: Users who need a single charger for multiple high‑power devices
products.skip_if: You only need to charge a single low‑power phone

products.name: Anker 735 Nano II 65W (3‑port)
why: The Anker 735 Nano II 65W is a 3‑port USB wall charger that includes two USB‑C ports and one USB‑A port. It can fast‑charge phones, tablets and laptops from a single brick. It was highlighted in TechGearLab’s head‑to‑head testing as the favorite multi‑port charger.
products.desc: The Anker 735 Nano II 65W is a 3‑port USB wall charger with two USB‑C ports and one USB‑A port, delivering up to 65W of power. It can charge phones, tablets and laptops simultaneously.
products.benefit: Picture a family kitchen where multiple devices need charging at once. The Anker 735 Nano II 65W lets you power a phone, tablet and laptop from one outlet, saving counter space. It outperforms single‑port chargers by offering three ports, but it is larger and heavier than the single‑port Nano II. The catch: it is bulkier than a single‑port charger.
products.best_for: Families or offices needing multiple devices charged at once
products.skip_if: You only need to charge one device

products.name: Apple 20W USB‑C
why: Apple’s 20W USB‑C charger is the recommended choice for iPhone users, offering a no‑drama, reliable charging experience. It is highlighted as the best pick for iPhone in the 2026 roundup.
products.desc: The Apple 20W USB‑C charger is a compact charger that delivers 20W of power via a USB‑C port. It is designed for iPhone users and provides fast charging for iPhones up to the 20W limit.
products.benefit: Picture an iPhone user who wants a simple, reliable charger that works out of the box. The Apple 20W USB‑C delivers fast charging for iPhones and is the only charger in this guide that is specifically tailored for Apple devices. It is less powerful than the Anker Nano II, but it is smaller and has no extra ports. The catch: it only supports 20W, so it cannot charge laptops efficiently.
products.best_for: iPhone users who want a simple, dedicated charger
products.skip_if: You need to charge laptops or multiple devices

verdict.line: Picture a busy commuter who needs a single brick to power a phone, tablet and a laptop. The Anker Nano II 65W delivers that with its GaN‑II PPS technology, charging a MacBook Air in under two hours and an iPhone 13 three times faster than the stock 5W charger. The catch: it has no USB‑A port, so older cables need a separate adapter.
